title: personal-llm-mini-tracker-olivia-2026
content:
Experiment mini-tracker (scratchpad) - quick rows for perf/cost checks

HEADER: exp_id, date, model, quant, batch_size, seq_len, cold_latency_ms_p50, steady_latency_ms_p50, tokens_per_sec, est_cost_per_1M_tokens_usd, notes

EXP-001, 2026-02-12, redwood-7b, fp16, 8, 2048, 120, 95, 2100, 6.5, baseline run on p4d, observed jitter when burst > 12rps
EXP-002, 2026-02-15, redwood-7b, q4_0, 16, 2048, 95, 80, 2600, 4.2, quantized -> ~25% perf gain, slight quality diffs on long prompts
EXP-003, 2026-02-18, llama2-13b, q4_k, 8, 8192, 420, 380, 850, 9.8, long-context heavy, KV cache warmup cost high; try prefix cache
EXP-004, 2026-02-22, redwood-13b, q3, 8, 4096, 220, 200, 1250, 7.1, reasonable tradeoff; memory headroom ok on a100-80g
EXP-005, 2026-02-25, redwood-7b, q4_0, 64, 512, 40, 35, 5000, 3.9, batching is effective at low seq_len; need to monitor latency SLO for interactive flows
EXP-006, 2026-03-01, redwood-mix-variant, dynamic-quant, 16, 2048, 110, 92, 2300, 5.1, prototype dynamic quant path; lower memory but slightly higher variance

Quick notes / methodology:
- All runs from dev cluster (us-west) on a100-80g unless noted.
- cold_latency = first-token after cache miss; steady_latency = p50 for tokens after warmup (30s window).
- est_cost based on reserved pricing + infra overhead (very rough).
- Quality check: evals on shotgun-prompt-set-v2 (50 prompts) - flag any BLEU/ROUGE/semantic regressions in notes.

Immediate findings (scratch):
- q4_0 gives biggest perf improvement for 7b with minimal quality loss on our prompt set (EXP-002, EXP-005).
- For long-context workloads (8k), q4_k on llama2 showed larger latency and KV warmup; consider caching prefixes or model shard changes (EXP-003).
- Large batch sizes (>32) help throughput but risk exceeding interactive SLOs — need autoscale policy test.

TODO / next steps (personal):
- [ ] Re-run EXP-002 with noise-seed variation (5 runs) and capture perf variance (target: p50 within 10% across runs).
- [ ] Add a column for quality_delta (semantic similarity) and link to eval outputs. (see CONFLUENCE-LLM-PROF-78)
- [ ] Try dynamic batching config: max_wait_ms=15 vs 30 for EXP-005 setup.
- [ ] Run EXP-006 on dedicated-dp (dedicated GPU pool) to measure cross-tenant interference.
- [ ] Draft quick one-pager summarizing wins for Hosted API ops (if stable) and put on product slack.

Random scratch / notes-to-self:
- Remember: compare tokens_per_sec normalized by seq_len and batch_size; raw tps can be misleading for short seq experiments.
- Check JIRA-8923 for the autoscale policy case study and see if we can reuse policy templates.
- If quantized quality issues persist, add small calibration dataset (50-100 prompts) and run calibrate-quant pipeline (script: tools/quant-calibrate.sh).

Pinned links:
- eval set: gs://redwood-evals/shotgun-prompt-set-v2.txt
- quick perf harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness (run: python run_perf.py --exp EXP-002)

-- end of mini-sheet (working doc)
